batch11.title: Batch FAISS face queries and resolve shared gallery identities together
batch11.body:
## Tickets
Self-contained search performance improvement.

## What has been done
A multi-face ANN search currently calls FAISS once per face and repeats gallery-name lookups for identities shared by those faces. This serializes independent HNSW queries and adds database round trips.

Submit the face embeddings as one FAISS query matrix, then resolve the unique matched identities together through the database adapter's existing lookup method. Preserve per-face result order, empty matches, thresholds, missing-neighbor filtering, requested limits, and facial-area metadata.

## How to test
Added real FAISS/SQLite integration coverage for normalized and unnormalized embeddings, verification and similarity searches, single and multiple faces, default and explicit limits, missing neighbors, empty batches, and shared identities. The numerical and returned-record results are compared with individual face searches.

[Validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/deepface/actions/runs/43858024543) on Python 3.10 and 3.12:
- Original production source: 13 regression failures and 15 passing controls.
- Updated source, including the adjacent FAISS missing-neighbor, face-order, and SQLite suites: 48 passed in each environment.
- Repository-pinned Pylint: 10.00/10; MyPy: 145 source files passed; test formatting passed.

The same run measures a real FAISS 1.16.0 HNSW index with 10,000 128-dimensional vectors, 128 query faces, k=20, and two FAISS threads. Across seven repeated complete datastore searches, median time changed from 36.42 to 22.23 ms on Python 3.10 and from 29.94 to 17.87 ms on Python 3.12. These measurements use precomputed synthetic embeddings and an actual SQLite gallery; they exclude face detection and neural inference. No timing threshold is asserted in the regression tests.
